Subject: DPA: model improvement & subprocessor gating

Soojín,

Thanks for taking this through legal. We reviewed the standard DPA and have a few substantive asks we need Redwood to confirm before we loop procurement in for signature:

1) No-adaptive-training: Medsure requires an explicit contractual prohibition on using our customer interactions to improve or update models (including derivatives for retraining). We need a warranty clause and an operational proof path.

2) Output ownership and derivatives: We expect generated outputs and prompt/response pairs to be licensed to Medsure with no downstream model-derivative rights retained by Redwood or subprocessors.

3) Subprocessor gating & approvals: Our procurement team needs the ability to approve any new subprocessor that will handle customer content. At minimum we need: a pre-notification window and a defined approval timeline.

4) Onshore routing for EU and APAC sensitive datasets: for certain classes of PHI-like telemetry, we may require onshore KMS or EU-only subprocessors.

I've attached our redlines (Medsure_DPA_redlines_v1.pdf) and a simple subprocessor inventory request. Can Redwood confirm a proposed cadence for pre-notification and whether you offer an account-level 'no-learning' toggle (operationally enforced)?

If easier, we can jump on a 30-minute call this week.

Thanks,
Elena Vasquez
Senior Counsel, Data & Privacy
Medsure Health

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks and the redlines. Quick summary of what we can commit and a practical path forward:

- No-adaptive-training: We can contractually commit that Medsure tenant data will not be used to update model weights or retrain models (no adaptive training). We propose the following contract language: "Redwood will not use Customer Content to improve, retrain, or fine-tune any models, nor will Redwood derive model updates from Customer Content, except as expressly permitted in a separate written agreement." Operationally, we will implement an account-level flag that prevents storage of customer interactions in training telemetry pipelines.

- Ownership / derivatives: We can grant Medsure an explicit license to outputs and log exports. We will not assert ownership of customer prompts or outputs; Redwood will retain operational telemetry for debugging unless redacted. We propose a clause to license outputs to the customer and commit not to create derivatives used in external model products.

- Subprocessor gating: We do support a pre-notification process. Standard is 30 days notice for a new subprocessor with an opt-out window for restrictive customers; we can shorten that to a 10-business-day review window for Medsure where a lack of objection will be treated as approval, or we can accept an explicit approval right with a 10-business-day SLA to respond. We need to discuss mutually agreeable language for the approval flow (notification, evidence pack, review timeline, and fallback if not approved).

- Onshore KMS / routing: We offer routing policies and KMS residency options. For EU-sensitive datasets, we can route encryption keys to an EU KMS and restrict certain processing to EU-located subprocessors. This requires a dedicated config and may have additional cost/ops steps.

I'll attach a concise proposal PDF with the exact suggested wording and options (redwood-proposal-dpa-20270929.pdf). Can we schedule a call Thursday or Friday to walk through the approval timeline and the precise contract language?

Best,
Soojín Lee
Head of Privacy & Compliance (Sales APAC/EU Liaison)
Redwood Inference

Soojín —

Thanks for the speedy reply and the proposal doc. A few follow-ups from legal and procurement after reviewing your suggested approach:

- No-adaptive-training language: The proposed clause is a good start. We need an explicit warranty and a remediation path if Redwood discovers an inadvertent inclusion of Medsure data in a training set. Suggested addition: a 30-day corrective action window and rights to audit certain artifacts if an incident is suspected.

- Derivatives/outputs: We need language that prevents Redwood or its subprocessors from using outputs to create product features or models that are offered to third parties. A license-to-customer for outputs plus a non-derivative covenant for Redwood/subprocessors is acceptable.

- Subprocessor approval: Procurement prefers an explicit approval right rather than passive consent-by-silence for higher-risk subprocessors (those with access to plaintext outputs). They ask that Redwood provide a list of currently planned subprocessors and commit to a 10-business-day review window after notification; if Medsure objects within that window, Redwood must not onboard the subprocessor for Medsure's data until objection is resolved. For lower-risk subprocessors (e.g., monitoring tools), Medsure is comfortable with 10-business-day notice + deemed approval.

- Evidence pack: please include links to SOC2 reports, subprocessors' country of processing, role description, and the minimum set of access controls (KMS access, key rotation).

I've attached our v2 redlines (Medsure_DPA_redlines_v2.pdf) with suggested tweaks; procurement would like a short call to lock timeline and get a signed statement on the onshore-KMS option and any associated cost.

Available Tuesday 10/5 or Wednesday 10/6 US west coast morning.

Regards,
Elena

Medsure Health
